URGENT - IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED
Typhoon Champi (29W) Local Statement
National Weather Service Tiyan GU
919 PM ChST Sat Oct 17 2026

...TYPHOON CHAMPI NOW A DANGEROUS CATEGORY 4 MOVING WEST TOWARDS
GUAM COASTAL WATERS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
Guam is now in Condition of Readiness 1 as of 1 PM ChST. Rota is now
in Typhoon Condition of Readiness 1 as of 5 PM ChST. Saipan and Tinian
remain in Typhoon Condition of Readiness 3.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions for
people on Guam and on Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the Northern
Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota. 

A Tropical Storm Warning and a Typhoon Watch continues for Tinian
and Saipan. 

A Flood Watch is in effect for Rota, Tinian and Saipan in the
Northern Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that
might be in effect for your area.

A Flash Flood Warning is now in effect for Guam.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 7 PM ChST...the center of Typhoon Champi (29W) was located
near latitude 12.6N...longitude 146.7E. This was about 140 miles
east-southeast of Guam. Storm motion was west, 280 degrees, at 15
mph. Storm intensity was 130 mph. This general forecast track 
will take Champi just south of Guam as a Category 4 typhoon as it 
intensifies further the next few days.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Typhoon Champi (29W) has been undergoing rapid intensification 
today. As a result it is now a dangerous category 4 typhoon. It is
expected to pass a little south of Guam as a super typhoon within
the next 12 hours. This may potentially bring devastating wind 
conditions to much of Guam during passage.

.PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

During the storm...stay inside and away from windows. Do not venture
outside when high winds are occurring or during temporary lulls as
flying debris can easily...and suddenly...cause serious injury.

Have a well-charged cell phone nearby...keeping network
communications as open as possible for emergencies.

Closely monitor NOAA weather radio or other local news outlets for
official storm information. Listen for possible changes to the
forecast.

&&

.NEXT UPDATE...
The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Tiyan around 3 AM ChST...or sooner if conditions
warrant. 

GUZ001-171930-
/O.CON.PGUM.TY.W.4029.000000T0000Z-000000T0000Z/
Guam-
919 PM ChST Sat Oct 17 2026

...TYPHOON WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT...

...PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

Dangerous typhoon conditions will soon occur. Everyone should be
quickly moving to safety within their home or shelter. Once
inside, ensure all windows and doors are secured before dangerous
winds arrive. Move to an interior room on the lowest floor.

Do not go outside into the eye of typhoons. Within the eye,
conditions can become temporarily calm, which can be misleading.
Once the eye passes, the winds will change direction and quickly
increase again to dangerous speeds.

Be aware that the loss of commercial power can happen quickly.
Keep emergency gear handy.

&&

...WIND INFORMATION...
As Typhoon Champi (29W) approaches, sustained Category 2 typhoon
force winds are imminent, and will increase to category 4 over the
next several hours. Maximum winds of 110 to 135 mph with gusts to
175 mph are expected. Winds are not forecast to fall below typhoon
force until late Sunday morning, and below tropical storm force until
late Sunday evening.

North winds of 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 mph will increase over
the next few hours. Early Sunday morning, the winds will turn east
and increase to 110 to 135 mph with gusts to 175 mph. Sunday afternoon
will see winds turning south and diminishing to tropical storm force.
Damaging winds will not leave Guam until Sunday night at the earliest.

Devastating damage will occur. Structural collapse of some non-
concrete homes could cause severe injuries or death. Most metal roof
homes are likely to be severely damaged. Some container homes will 
be destroyed or severely damaged, leaving them uninhabitable. Flying 
and falling debris will pose a significant threat to life, or even 
death, to those venturing outside. Signage, some fences and canopies 
will be destroyed. Island-wide power loss is likely to occur, 
potentially for days or weeks, as power lines and power plants 
sustain significant damage. These power outages are likely to turn 
off public utility water pumps, so water outages may develop across 
the island if power outages continue for days or weeks. Shutters 
MUST be used for non-typhoon-resistant windows, as they are likely 
to shatter and bring in destructive winds indoors, which could cause 
severe injuries or death to those exposed. If landfall occurs over 
southern Guam, those venturing outside are at risk of severe injury
or DEATH from flying and falling debris. Do NOT risk your life!

...COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Hazardous surf will continue to increase, with dangerously large 
breaking waves 30 to 35 feet likely by early Sunday along shores
directly exposed to the center of the system, as Champi makes its 
closest approach. Significant coastal inundation upwards of 5 to 7 
feet is expected, especially along eastern and southern exposures as 
Champi passes. If Champi crosses over Guam, significant wave run-up
is expected to build in along west exposures, including rising 
waters within Apra Harbor. If Champi passes south of Guam, impacts
to western coasts will be significantly lower.

Do NOT venture out into the waters during passage of Typhoon Champi.
Surf and rip currents WILL BE DEADLY. Most typhoon-related deaths 
occur in the waters or along the shores. Storm surge is likely to 
come in fast and wipe out any infrastructure at points of peak 
exposure. Getting trapped in the waves WILL be life-threatening. Do 
NOT risk your life!

...OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
A Flash Flood Warning is in effect for Guam. See the latest forecast
for more information. Be ready to act if flooding rains occur.

Torrential rain could dump 8 to 14 inches of rain over Guam over the
duration of the event, especially if the system makes landfall. 
Excessive runoff is expected to result in flash flooding of rivers, 
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flash 
flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains and
ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive street flooding 
and flooding of creeks and rivers is likely.

$$

MPZ001-171930-
/O.CON.PGUM.TY.W.4029.000000T0000Z-000000T0000Z/
Rota-
919 PM ChST Sat Oct 17 2026

...TYPHOON WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT...

...PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

Tropical storm conditions will soon occur. Get to safe shelter now if
you are not already there. Everyone should remain alert and stay
inside.

Listen for possible flood warnings.

&&

...WIND INFORMATION...
As Typhoon Champi (29W) approaches, sustained Tropical Storm
force winds are imminent. Maximum winds of 40 to 60 mph with
gusts to 90 mph are expected. Winds are not forecast to fall
below tropical storm force until late Sunday evening.

North winds of 20 to 30 mph with gusts to 40 mph will soon increase
significantly as Champi approaches, with southeast tropical storm- 
force winds of of 40 to 60 mph with gusts to 90 mph developing 
quickly tonight. As Champi moves away to the west or west-northwest
Sunday, winds will decrease back down to borderline tropical
storm-force conditions Sunday evening.

Moderate to significant damage to some metal roof homes is likely, 
especially those that have canopies, awnings, or carports. Poorly 
constructed homes are likely to sustain partial roof removal, with 
some wall damage. Flying and falling debris may pose a significant 
threat to life, or even death, to those venturing outside. Signage, 
some fences and canopies are likely to be severely damaged. Island-
wide power outages are likely, potentially for days, as power lines 
and power plants sustain damage. These power outages are likely to 
turn off public utility water pumps, so water outages may develop 
across the islands if power outages continue for days. Shutters MUST 
be used for non-typhoon-resistant windows, as they may shatter and 
pose a life threatening risk to those both outside and inside during 
the passage of Champi.

...COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Hazardous surf will continue to increase significantly, with 
dangerously large breaking waves upwards of 25 feet expected to 
develop along all shores of Rota Sunday. In addition, significant 
coastal inundation upwards of 3 to 4 feet is expected especially 
along eastern and southern exposures as Champi approaches.

...OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
A Flood Watch is in effect for the entire area. See latest
forecast for latest information. Listen for possible flood
warnings for your location...and be ready to act if flooding
rains occur. 

As Champi continues to intensify and eventually move across the
Marianas, torrential rain could dump 5 to 8 inches of rain at Rota
over the duration of the event. Excessive runoff may result in
flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban
areas. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.
Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers is
possible.

MPZ002-003-171930-
/O.CON.PGUM.TR.W.4029.000000T0000Z-000000T0000Z/
/O.CON.PGUM.TY.A.4029.000000T0000Z-000000T0000Z/
Tinian-Saipan-
919 PM ChST Sat Oct 17 2026

...TROPICAL STORM WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT...
...TYPHOON WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT...

...PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...
Take small loose objects indoors. Identify suitable shelter. Stock
up a few days worth of food and water. If no concrete shelter is
available look for a cave or something similar. Take action to
protect food crops or other possessions as appropriate.

&&

...WIND INFORMATION...
Northeast winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts to 45 mph will increase
significantly as Champi continues to approach, with tropical storm-
force winds of of 30 to 50 mph with gusts to 80 mph developing 
quickly after midnight. Then, winds will pivot to the southeast as 
Sunday morning continues. As Champi starts to move away to the west
or west-northwest, damaging winds are expected to subside late Sunday.

Minor damage to some metal roof homes is possible, especially those 
that have canopies, awnings, or carports. Flying and falling debris 
may cause injuries to those venturing outside. Signage and canopies 
may be damaged. Scattered to island-wide power outages are possible,
as power lines sustain damage. Shutters MUST be used for non- 
typhoon-resistant windows, as they may shatter and pose a life 
threatening risk to those both outside and inside during the passage 
of Champi.

...COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Hazardous surf is expected to continue to increase, with dangerously
large breaking waves upwards of 20 feet expected to develop along 
eastern and southern shores of Tinian and Saipan Sunday. In addition,
significant coastal inundation of 1 to 3 feet is expected as Champi 
makes its way across the Marianas.

...OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
A Flood Watch is in effect for the entire area. See latest
forecast for latestinformation. Listen for possible flood
warnings for your location...and be ready to act if flooding
rains occur. 

As Champi continues to intensify and move across the Marianas,
locally heavy showers could dump 3 to 5 inches of rain at Tinian and
Saipan over the duration of the event, especially if outer rainbands
train over Tinian and Saipan. Excessive runoff may result in flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone 
locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. 
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Extensive
street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers are possible.
